turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Ms. Hale. I have until 4:40. Why was my son's zero entered before anyone called me?
The checker said 94 percent. That's the end of it.
A machine's guess. The company that sells it says not to use it alone, and your own procedure, 4.3, says the same. So what else do you have, Hale, or is that all of it?
I don't need more proof than that.
"Don't need." Okay. Then you can explain that to the principal, because that's where I'm going when we're done. Withdraw the zero, apologize to my son, and tell me why nobody called me first.
The software doesn't lie, unlike some people.
"Some people." I'm writing that down. My son doesn't lie, so if you're calling him one, or me, say it plainly and say what you're basing it on.

"Stands." On what basis, Hale, and decided by whom? I want it in an email tonight, with the rule you're relying on. Because the rule I printed from your school's website says you speak to the student first and call me before any mark goes in.
